trendAnalysis.outlook: After a mild seasonal softening through late September/early October, the kwacha steadied in the 6 October session and edged firmer across the basket. The USD/ZMW market mid sits at ~K19.7425 (open.er-api.com, 6 Oct) versus ~K19.7465 the prior snapshot — essentially flat — while the BoZ official mid printed at K19.75. The day's move was broad and mildly kwacha-positive: GBP (26.0977, −0.77%), EUR (22.1301, −1.76%), BWP (1.3815, −1.75%) and ZAR (1.1859, −1.59%) all cost fewer kwacha, with USD flat and CNY (2.9403) also steady. The pair remains near the upper edge of the broad 18.40–19.80 consolidation band, but the recent direction has turned from softening back toward stability. The policy backdrop remains the 30 September 250bps MPR cut to 10.75% — the lowest in several years — which trims the carry support that buoyed the kwacha earlier in 2026. Import demand, softer copper-price swings and the pace of further BoZ easing are the near-term risks; IMF successor-programme talks and the 2027 budget shape the medium-term path.
trendAnalysis.projection3m: USD/ZMW 18.50–19.80 range. Post-election policy continuity and IMF talks supportive; softer policy rate, import demand and copper-price swings the main risks.
trendAnalysis.projection6m: USD/ZMW 18.00–20.00 range. Direction hinges on fiscal continuity, copper earnings and the pace of further BoZ easing.
